newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold closes up on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold closes up on overseas buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold edged a shade higher from its New York close on Tuesday, with gold traders reporting lethargic two-way activity and small-scale buying in a dull market.

"Because the market has been closing lower, people are afraid to sell short," said one gold trader at an international bank. "But since they don't want to buy either in a dropping market they're just watching to see what happens."
Some gold traders reported marginal buying interest from the Tokyo Commodities Exchange (TOCOM) as players there speculated on the dollar.
Bullion ended at US$383.10/60 an ounce Wednesday against New York's US$383.00/40 close on Tuesday.
Local gold ended HK$5 higher at HK$3,532 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society fixed at -1.50 on Wednesday, up from -3 on Tuesday.
Tael gold was trading at about US$382.90-383.40 per ounce.
As there was not much trade going on in the loco London market, arbitrage between the tael and spot markets had also been quiet, gold traders said.
Some players were heard selling small amounts of tael gold and buying on the loco London on Tuesday, traders said.
